_comment: Running list of player-facing patch notes for the NEXT release. As work ships, append entries here. The patch-notes skill rolls this into Assets/data/patchnotes.json on release and clears pending. Categories: feature, balance, fix, polish, content.

entries.line: Five new beasts join the Beastbook (#16–20): Gnoll → Gnollium (a forest gnome line drawn from European hidden-folk myth), Jackacabra (a chupacabra-hare shadow predator that slips into Weaverton's pastures at dusk to raid the Sheepot flocks), and Padlip → Liliprince (a frog-prince line based on the Brothers Grimm tale — Water until the curse breaks, then Water/Spirit). All five by Jet.

Region identity pass — the three launch zones now share a single story. Saltmoor Cove → Weaverton, the wool-and-loom village built around the Sheepot trade. The Witherwood → Weaverwood, the dye-leaf forest east of town where the herders take their flocks each summer. Old Saltmoor → Weavermere, the mirror-still pond above Weaverton where the village's painters and dye-masters chase the colors no loom can match.

AI-generated wild beasts retired pre-launch — the Beastbook is now a tighter, all-handmade roster. The starter pool, the Weaverwood, and the Weavermere now spawn only handmade species (the old AI-gen beasts still exist in the species DB so prior contracts don't break, just hidden from the book).

Weaverwood (Lv 10) is now the Gnoll/Jackacabra hunting ground — Gnoll spawns wild, Jackacabra prowls the wood's edge raiding Sheepot flocks, and Wishlift + Twincoil drift in from the village pasture. Gnollium is evo-only or boss-roll; Liliprince is boss-only at Weavermere.

Side quests + trade nodes retuned around the new handmade roster — the Weaverwood now offers a Jackacabra cull bounty, a Gnollcap tribute, a Twincoil weave, and the Weavermere's three artist NPCs (Painter Selene, Dye-Master Wren, the Wandering Poet) trade Padlip pondlight motes for relics, dye recipes, and verses.

Beastbook grid no longer stretches non-square monster art — Seraphiel and Aurael, whose source canvases are wider than they are tall, are now rendered at proper proportion instead of being squashed/stretched into a 180x180 box. Aurael in particular shows much more wing/halo/blade detail.

Day 7 streak reward swapped from a Legendary beast to a Master Ink — guaranteed contract on your next attempt. The legendary tier isn't live in open beta yet, so the old reward couldn't actually be granted in any meaningful form.

Beastbook #1–19 balance pass — growth rates raised across the launch roster so beasts level up faster, BSTs reined in to fit their rarity bands (Gnoll/Gnollium/Padlip trimmed, Liliprince pushed up to Rare-tier parity), Jackacabra contract rate eased to 0.35. Jackacabra now learns a signature move Goatsucker's Drain (Lv 38) — heals for 50% of damage dealt — and Liliprince learns a signature Sovereign's Boon (Lv 55) — 90-power Spirit special that heals the caster 25%.

Five new flavor signature moves for Beastbook #10–14: Sheepot learns Pot Guard (Lv 21, raises DEF + SpD), Cerametz learns Solstice Veil (Lv 38, heals 33% wrapped in solstice fleece), Wishlift learns Dream Drift (Lv 19, drifts a spent-wish bubble across the foe's eyes for sleep), Twincoil learns Two-Faced Strike (Lv 19, the outer head bites + the inner head hexes, guaranteed -1 ATK), and Heartwell learns Inner Stillness (Lv 21, the sokushinbutsu monk's meditation — heals 33% and cleanses status). Gothsire's late movelist also retuned: whirlpool_surge moved to Lv 40 as a proper Water capstone, current_boost slid down to Lv 26 where it actually gets used.

Embark popup completely redesigned in the Persona-stamp battle-UI dialect — team slots now show big sprite art carved into a diagonal slab on the left, italic-skewed display name on the right, gold Lv pill, gold-edged element badges, and a prominent HP bar. Reads as a sibling of the battle nameplates instead of a generic list row.

Embark popup roster now actually fits 5+ beasts per row at full card size — was previously clipping the 5th card on a row of 4 due to a stack of three engine quirks (a transformed ancestor, a ghost hover-scale on the cards, and a stale `overflow: hidden` on the world map container) that all conspired to collapse the available width. Layout's been rebuilt to dodge all three.

Embark popup no longer teleports from the top-left to the center on open. The entrance animation was authored back when the modal centered via a transform offset; switching to flex-centering left the offset stuck on the keyframes, sending the modal to the corner for 0.22s before it snapped back.

Wishlift gains an evolution — Wishstar (#13, Wind/Spirit, Rare). When a Wishlift carries enough wishes home the wishes outweigh her, and what falls out the other side is a king with a planet for a body and a sun for a crown — each continent etched across him is a dream that found its way back. Evolves at Lv 32. Art by Spookior.
Achievement descriptions now use 'Contract' terminology throughout — 'Contract your first monster', 'Contract 100 monsters', etc. — consistent with the rest of the game.
Removed loyalty references from UI to match current design (loyalty system was retired pre-launch).
Fixed Branchling's description, which contained unfilled template placeholders from an earlier data pass.
Achievement panel and Shop now use the Persona-stamp dialect on their hero CTAs (Claim All / Buy buttons) and titles.
Mini-expeditions added — short optional adventures that branch off the main path and offer exclusive rewards. The first one unlocks after clearing Weavermere.
Tuned XP yields across the launch roster — wild encounters now grant XP appropriate to their rarity and evolution stage.
Rarity bands rebalanced — Epic now sits properly above Rare in the stat ladder. A new beast line lands in the new Epic band, waiting somewhere off the path above Weavermere.
New beast line added — descend into a hidden mini-expedition near Weavermere to find them.
Whispering Hollow mini-expedition marker tooltip no longer clips off the left map edge — tooltip now anchors to the right of the pin instead of above it.

Clicking a mini-expedition on the world map now opens a full detail panel (drops, beasts, level, waves, boss) before you embark — same flow as main zones. Loomweaver's detail card shows a 'Cannot Contract' tag since it's evo-only.
Whispering Hollow now hosts a varied wild pool — Threadlet shares the cave with Cerametz, Twincoil, and Wishlift.
Threadlet now appears as a rarer wild encounter in Whispering Hollow.
Removed an empty Adventure Wave radio station entry — expedition music context is reserved and will be filled when tracks are ready.

Battle status indicators redesigned with clearer icons and color coding — Burn, Freeze, Paralyze, Poison, Sleep, and Confuse each have a distinct icon and tinted badge instead of generic emoji glyphs. Breeding panel egg icon updated to match the game's icon style.

Burn and Poison hit harder — Burn now ticks for 1/15 of MaxHP per turn (was 1/20) and Poison ticks for 1/10 (was 1/12). Status conditions are meaningful pressure again, especially in longer boss fights.
Internal save migration cleanup — minor save-load speedup.
Threadlet line text polish — clearer signature move descriptions and a small description tune.
Evolutions now play a proper transformation sound instead of a generic UI click.
Cleaned up unused leaderboard categories that weren't surfacing meaningful data.

Guild officers with pending join requests can now actually see them — the Invite button correctly opens the join requests list when requests are pending, instead of always jumping to the invite-player picker. The Invite Player option is still accessible via a button inside the requests panel.

Pending guild join requests panel refreshed — stamped title, bordered request cards with left accent and stagger entrance animation, ACCEPT/DENY buttons in the Beastborne dialect, and time-since timestamps replacing the stale ranked RP display.

Invite Player picker refreshed — header icon, close button, online indicator dot, level badge for offline friends, and empty-state messaging. Both the picker and the requests panel now share the same card chrome (dark solid border, offset purple drop shadow).
Guild invites can now reach friends you've previously played with — not just tamers in your current lobby. Online friends show a green dot; offline friends show their level.
Dewdrop joins the handmade roster — a small round waterdrop with a single leaf for a cap, now Water/Nature dual-typed. Drifts across Weavermere alongside Padlip and the other pond wilds. Art by Jet.

Staticling renamed to Staiju and given a sharper sprite — a sleek dark cat that crackles with cyan lightning, sleeps in trees through clear weather, and prowls the air during storms. Old saves carrying a Staticling will auto-update to Staiju on next load. Art by Jet.

Stomplet → Skunkape — a new bigfoot shepherd line walks the Weaverwood. Stomplet is the young leafy giant who tends the Sheepot flocks; Skunkape is the elder, mossy and leaf-crowned. Contract a Stomplet in the forest and evolve it at Lv 32. Art by Jet.

Repaired expedition achievement milestones — 'Clear all expeditions' (Conqueror) now actually unlocks at 3 zones cleared instead of 16, and the Weaverwood and Weavermere step achievements now trigger correctly. Hard Mode equivalents fixed to match.
Skunkape's Beastbook evolution chain now correctly shows Stomplet as its pre-evolution.
Staiju now drops a Storm Whisker on defeat and appears at Beastbook #26.
Skill tree SP counter now just shows your available skill points instead of a confusing X / total fraction. The number is the SP you have to spend, no hidden cap.
Element colors normalized — Nature is consistently emerald-green, Wind is consistently slate-gray. Pills, gradients, and borders now match their element icons across every panel.

Burn, Poison, Paralyze, and Freeze status effects now actually persist turn-over-turn instead of self-clearing after a single tick. The recent status damage buff (Burn 1/15, Poison 1/10) now delivers as designed.
Fixed a buggy evolution-upgrade entry on the Duskstalker line that had Umbral Claw evolving into itself — harmless no-op cleaned up.
Pollen Burst now actually does what its description says — 10% chance to poison the target, in line with other Nature/toxin moves.
Dual-type beasts (Dewdrop, Cerametz, Wishstar, Liliprince, Manehelm, Lochmaw, Twincoil, Loomweaver) now show both element badges in the roster and team-picker card views, not just their primary type.
Loomweaver's Beastbook entry now shows a 'Cannot Contract' badge alongside its rarity — it's evolution-only, so this was previously missing context for players who found it in the book.

Stomplet and Skunkape rebalanced into proper Uncommon and Rare bands. Stomplet picks up Sapling Stomp at Lv 21 (60-power Nature physical that hardens the user's stance). Skunkape gets Shepherd's Vigil at Lv 55 (90-power Nature special that pulls life back into the caster).

Dewdrop and Staiju movesets refreshed to match their identities. Dewdrop's moveset rebuilt around its actual identity — a leaf-capped waterdrop bobbing on still ponds at dawn. Dropped the off-brand ocean/striking moves (no limbs, no surf), traded for pond-mist Water specials (Tidal Pulse, Waterlog, Monsoon Call, Deep Pressure), dawn-light Spirit moves (Spirit Breeze, Aether Pulse), a dawn-mist Wind shield (Gust Shield Lv 22), and the new signature Leafcap Drift at Lv 28 (50-power Nature special, 30% to put the foe to sleep — the leaf-cap dipping forward and the pondsteam doing the rest). Staiju sheds its old broken-machines moveset for storm-cat predator flavor — picks up Lightning Fang L8 and Storm Talon L22, and gains a signature Skyfall Pounce at Lv 32 (85-power Electric physical that strikes first, 20% to paralyze). Staiju's personality updated to match the new identity.

Roster-wide moveset lore audit — every learnable move now has a clear reason that specific beast would know it. Wishlift sheds claw and tackle moves she doesn't have (she drifts on dream-bubbles, not pounces) and picks up Spirit Breeze + Aether Pulse for the dream-light fae flavor. Heartwell, the sokushinbutsu monk under the village fountain, drops his striking moves for the calm vow they belie — gains Aether Pulse (the patient pulse that always lands) and Deep Pressure (the well's settled weight). Padlip the pondfrog sheds ocean-flavored moves (he lives in lily-pads, not the sea) and picks up Tidal Pulse for the throat-sac vibration plus Aqua Shield for the bubble around his body. Cherune the novice cherub trades a feint-jab for Spirit Breeze — guardians leave warmth, not stings.

Heartwell and Twincoil — both standalone Commons that never evolve — got a stat-band lift toward the middle of their tier. Heartwell (BST 267 → 297) leans deeper into the sokushinbutsu monk's identity with more HP and SpD; the well's weight is harder to disturb now. Twincoil (BST 263 → 290) gains a touch more bite and serpentine quickness across the board. Both feel viable into mid-game instead of falling off the moment the player's starter mid-evolves.

Trait pills now show a unique icon per trait — Kindle Heart gets a campfire, Phantom Step gets footprints, Trickster gets a masquerade mask, Lightning Rod gets an antenna, and so on across the full 38-trait roster.

Strict moveset lore pass across the full launch roster — every learnable move now defends itself against the beast's specific identity. Timid beasts stopped learning Intimidate (Sheepot, Pagefin, Stomplet, Wishlift, Cherune); brooding-loyal beasts stopped 'wrath' and 'annihilate' moves that clashed with their patience (Cerametz, Gnollium, Skunkape, Manehelm sentinel); freshwater pond-monks stopped saltwater 'brine/sea/tidal-ward' moves (Heartwell, Liliprince); a king who sleeps standing stopped learning Agility Boost and Tornado Dive (Wishstar); a TIMID flame-foal stopped war-crying (Embrik). Replacements stay in-pool but lean into each beast's actual description — Sheepot picks up Parasite Spore for its fragile-root underside, Skunkape's elder-shepherd kit gets Bloom Burst / Verdant Edge / Overgrowth Slam instead of generic 'crushing/vicious/annihilate' verbs, Wishstar gains Calm Air to match its standing-sleep, Heartwell picks up Warding Hymn + Spirit Link for the monk's vows, and Cherune gets Luminous Wall + Aether Pulse for the guardian-cherub identity that awakens fully at evolution. Dewdrop's Nature dual-typing gets a light touch — the leaf-cap learns Nature Shield (Lv 20, the leaf curls over the drop) and Blade Leaf (Lv 23, leaf-flick edge) on top of the existing Leafcap Drift signature, while keeping its sturdy pond-water core intact.
